title: Communication Network Model
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Organizational Analytics
description: Side-by-side comparison of two ways to model the same communication data in a graph: aggregate edges (one weighted edge per pair) and event-level edges (one timestamped edge per message). Includes an edge count toggle and a time window filter.

learningObjectives: Differentiate between aggregate and event-level communication edge models, analyzing the trade-offs of each approach
prerequisites: Edge properties in the labeled property graph model

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Side-by-side comparison with prediction and filtering
keyQuestions: How many edges does each model need for the same messages?
Which questions need timestamps on individual edges?
What trend does the aggregate model hide?
commonMisconceptions: An aggregate edge can be filtered by date after the fact
More edges always means a better model
assessmentOpportunities: Recommend an edge model for a stated analytics question and justify the trade-off
